promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Glucagon raises blood glucose principally by stimulating:
options: Glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis in the liver
The conversion of glucose to fat
questions.explain: Glucagon promotes breakdown of glycogen (glycogenolysis) and synthesis of glucose from non-carbohydrate sources (gluconeogenesis) in the liver.

questions.q: Antibodies passed from mother to baby in breast milk give the baby:
questions.explain: The antibodies are received naturally (via milk/placenta) and the baby does not make them itself, so it is natural passive immunity.

questions.q: During phagocytosis of a pathogen, the engulfed microbe is destroyed when:
options: A phagosome fuses with a lysosome and lysozymes hydrolyse the pathogen
Antibodies are released into the cytoplasm
questions.explain: The pathogen is enclosed in a phagosome which fuses with a lysosome; lytic enzymes (lysozymes) then digest it.

questions.q: Ultrafiltration in the renal glomerulus occurs because:
options: Active transport pushes plasma into the Bowman's capsule
The afferent arteriole is wider than the efferent arteriole, lowering pressure
High hydrostatic blood pressure forces small molecules through the basement membrane, which acts as a filter
Plasma proteins are actively secreted into the filtrate
questions.explain: High pressure (helped by a narrower efferent arteriole) forces water and small solutes through the basement membrane, which holds back proteins and cells.

questions.q: In a fish gill, the counter-current flow of water and blood is efficient because:
options: Blood and water flow in the same direction, equalising oxygen quickly
It allows carbon dioxide to be reabsorbed into the blood
Water flows faster than blood, reversing the gradient
A diffusion gradient for oxygen is maintained across the entire length of the lamella
questions.explain: Counter-current flow keeps the oxygen concentration of water higher than that of blood along the whole gill lamella, maintaining a diffusion gradient throughout.

questions.q: Which process in the nitrogen cycle returns nitrogen gas to the atmosphere, reducing soil fertility?
questions.explain: Denitrifying bacteria in anaerobic soils convert nitrate back to nitrogen gas, lowering soil nitrogen.

questions.q: Depolarisation during an action potential is caused by:
options: Potassium ions diffusing out of the axon
Voltage-gated sodium channels opening and Na+ flooding into the axon
questions.explain: At threshold, voltage-gated Na+ channels open and Na+ rushes in, making the inside positive (depolarisation).

questions.q: Why is so little energy transferred between successive trophic levels?
options: Decomposers add energy at each level
Energy is lost through respiration, heat, and indigestible or uneaten material
All energy is converted to oxygen
questions.explain: Much energy is lost as heat in respiration and in material that is not eaten or not digested.

questions.q: In the nitrogen cycle, which process converts atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia or ammonium ions?
questions.explain: Nitrogen fixation, carried out by bacteria such as Rhizobium and Azotobacter, converts N2 into ammonia.

questions.q: In a pregnancy test, monoclonal antibodies are used to:
options: Bind specifically to the hCG hormone, giving a coloured line when present
questions.explain: Mobile antibodies bind hCG and are then trapped by immobilised antibodies in the test window, producing a visible coloured line.

questions.q: Self-antigens normally do not trigger an immune response because:
options: Lymphocytes that would respond to the body's own antigens are destroyed or suppressed during development
They are too small to be detected
questions.explain: During development, lymphocytes complementary to self-antigens undergo clonal deletion or suppression, preventing autoimmune attack.

questions.q: Which sampling technique is most appropriate for estimating the population of a non-motile plant such as clover in a field?
questions.explain: Random quadrats are ideal for sessile organisms like plants, where individuals can be counted in a known area.
